title: Daily Market Digest
subtitle: Market Update: Review of Friday, August 15, 2026

items.headline: U.S. Stocks Edge Lower on Friday Amid Weak Retail Sales and AI Valuation Concerns
items.summary: U.S. stock markets closed lower on Friday, August 15, 2026, pulling back from recent highs as investors reacted to weaker-than-expected retail sales and consumer sentiment data. Persistent concerns over high valuations in AI-related stocks and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East also weighed on sentiment. Despite the daily decline, both the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite managed to secure their third consecutive weekly gains. Not financial advice.

items.headline: Reddit Surges on S&P 500 Inclusion News
items.summary: Reddit ($RDDT) surged almost 13% to trade near $179 after the social media company was announced as a new addition to the S&P 500 index, effective August 18.

items.headline: SanDisk Extends Gains on Positive Outlook
items.summary: Memory chip maker SanDisk ($SNDK) extended its gains by 7.39%, closing at $1,641.11, following upbeat long-term guidance and a commitment to repurchasing shares.

items.headline: Applied Materials Dips Despite Upbeat Forecast
items.summary: Applied Materials ($AMAT) fell 5.1% on Friday, as its upbeat quarterly forecast failed to meet high investor expectations amidst broader concerns about AI stock valuations.

items.headline: eToro Sees Significant Weekly Decline on Revenue Drop
items.summary: Trading and investing platform eToro Group ($ETOR) was a notable loser, down 18.90% to $28.58 for the week, after its second-quarter revenue declined significantly due to a fall in cryptoasset revenue.

items.headline: Weak Retail Sales and Consumer Sentiment Impact Market
items.summary: July retail sales data came in weaker than expected, and the University of Michigan's preliminary consumer sentiment survey for August also missed forecasts (51 vs. 54.5 expected). This softer economic data contributed to the day's market pullback.

items.headline: Energy and Utilities Lead, Tech and Health Lag on Friday
items.summary: The S&P 500 energy index rallied 1.4%, with energy and utilities leading sector gainers, up 1.36% and 0.55% respectively, tracking higher oil prices. In contrast, health and technology sectors led the laggards, losing 0.6% and 0.42% respectively, as investors reevaluated AI spending expectations.

items.headline: Middle East Tensions Drive Oil Prices Higher, Add to Market Pessimism
items.summary: Ongoing geopolitical tensions, including reports of more ships attacked and a near standstill of transit through the Strait of Hormuz, pushed oil prices higher and added to overall market pessimism. Brent crude hovered around $89 a barrel.

items.headline: Fed Rate Hike Concerns Ease Slightly Following Economic Data
items.summary: Markets now anticipate a roughly 30% chance of a September rate hike, a notable decrease from earlier in the week, as recent economic data suggesting a cooling economy eases some Federal Reserve tightening concerns.
